statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit of representative public Nuxt templates and journeys.

page.notes: Public multilingual streaming catalogue with responsive desktop/mobile shells, listing, detail, download, auth sheet, and PWA service worker.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The emulated dark preference matched, computed color-scheme was dark, and root/body backgrounds were rgb(16,17,20).
The reduced-motion query matched and getAnimations() returned no active animations after load.
Text and controls remain visible with distinct system colors in forced-colors and increased contrast.
The UI probe found no view-transition usage on the Nuxt experience; page changes use ordinary navigation/state swaps.
No scroll-linked/parallax/reveal animation was present, so there is no scroll-handler implementation to assess.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative pages contain ordinary scrolling but no scroll-linked animation.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The UI probe found zero scroll-snap containers while the hero uses custom previous/next buttons and 8x8 indicator buttons.
The 6,633px home page and 4,328px movie listing retain static header/footer chrome; the UI probe found no scroll-state mechanism.
No tooltip or viewport-edge popover requiring anchored positioning was present on the audited public paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Active navigation, selected category tabs, section headings, and clear listing-to-detail hierarchy consistently indicate location.

The mobile view dedicates most of the viewport to the hero and media rows, with compact persistent navigation.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After 10 next/previous cycles, DOM nodes fell 4533 to 4529 and used heap fell 32.0MB to 18.3MB; no monotonic growth appeared.

paths.description: Homepage and catalogue shell: primary discovery surface, desktop/mobile layout, preferences, accessibility, network, performance, security, privacy, and memory.
Movie listing archetype representing browsable category pages.
Movie detail and primary Watch Online journey.
App download landing page representing promotional/content instructions.
Arabic localized home route representing RTL and translation behavior.
Intentional 404 route representing HTTP/network failure recovery.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The UI probe found no view-transition usage on the Nuxt experience; page changes use ordinary navigation/state swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document and cross-document View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages use static chrome rather than scroll-aware navigation
findings.evidence: The 6,633px home page and 4,328px movie listing retain static header/footer chrome; the UI probe found no scroll-state mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky, shrinking header or a lightweight scroll progress/position affordance.

findings.summary: Transient and account controls are built from generic divs
findings.evidence: The language/account probes found no popover or dialog primitives; the Log in trigger is a DIV without a role and opens a fixed custom sheet.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for triggers and popover/dialog for transient and modal surfaces, including native focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Reusable cards adapt only at page breakpoints
findings.evidence: The computed UI probe found zero elements with a non-normal container type despite cards being reused across desktop, mobile, and side panels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/list containers container-type and adapt children with @container rules.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are inadequate
findings.evidence: Focus-visible elements commonly compute to outline-style none, the search input has a transparent outline, and carousel indicators are 8x8px unnamed buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear :focus-visible rings and enlarge interactive targets to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The 404 recovery control is not a real link
findings.evidence: The 404 route returns HTTP 404 and visibly offers Back Home, but the DOM probe found zero links, leaving recovery dependent on a custom click handler.
findings.suggestedFix: Render Back Home as an <a href="/"> and preserve a clear title and focus target.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP is far outside the good range
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 16.5s, FCP 4.7s, Speed Index 8.5s, and performance 0.57; the separate trace still measured LCP 2.67s, showing material variability.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce initial media, and verify field/median LCP under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The initial page delivers a large, fragmented critical load
findings.evidence: HAR captured 239 requests and 6.10MB transferred, including 18 parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets and many large uncached images.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical resources, cache immutable media, and explicitly prioritise only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Avoidable JavaScript and third-party work ships on first load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 147,058 bytes of unused JavaScript; HAR recorded 42 scripts and 193 third-party requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and intent, and load advertising/analytics dependencies only after consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Core controls and images lack accessible names
findings.evidence: axe reported critical button-name and image-alt violations; carousel indicators are empty buttons, and Lighthouse also found unnamed links and an untitled frame.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a stable accessible name, mark decorative images presentational, add meaningful alt text, and title frames.

findings.summary: Secondary text fails WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: axe measured 3.85:1 for the TV badge and 3.14:1 for Android TV text against dark surfaces, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise secondary foreground tokens to meet WCAG AA in every theme.

findings.summary: Landmarks and focus treatment are incomplete
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark and content outside landmarks; the custom focus probe found focus-visible elements with no painted outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one <main>, semantic navigation landmarks, logical headings, and a consistent visible focus ring.

findings.summary: Mobile users are prevented from zooming
findings.evidence: The viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no; axe and Lighthouse flag this as critical.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable=no so browser zoom remains available.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and network errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured CORS failures, a Nuxt hydration mismatch, a failed ad script promise, and inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove hydration mismatches, handle failed optional requests, and stop or isolate broken third-party scripts.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: The images primitive found width and height absent on all 100 sampled images and 15 below-fold images not lazy-loaded; Lighthouse also found low-resolution image delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and lazy-load below-fold media with suitable responsive sources.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent
findings.evidence: robots.txt allows crawling, but /sitemap.xml returns 404 and Lighthouse reports invalid hreflang despite alternate locale links.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap and validate reciprocal, absolute hreflang/canonical mappings for every localized route.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie protections are missing
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are all absent. mb_token is not Secure or HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive CSP and HSTS, add defensive headers, and issue authentication cookies Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriately SameSite.

findings.summary: The first load has an expansive third-party footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker/HAR evidence found 14 third-party origins, Google Tag Manager, 193 third-party requests, and 5.81MB transferred cross-origin, including ad-tech-like domains.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential vendors, gate analytics/ads behind consent and intent, and proxy or self-host essential static assets where appropriate.

findings.summary: The Arabic locale is only partially translated
findings.evidence: The Arabic route correctly sets lang=ar, dir=rtl and has no overflow, but visible UI still includes English strings such as Popular Series, Get MovieBox, MovieBox App, and Android TV.
findings.suggestedFix: Move every user-facing string into locale resources and add pseudo-locale/RTL regression coverage.

findings.summary: Media and decoration exceed a proportionate first-load budget
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 6.10MB, including a 965KB decorative SVG, a 476KB GIF, and many 225-418KB PNGs; 193 requests were third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace heavy decorative assets with compact responsive formats, defer offscreen media, and set a route-level transfer budget.

findings.summary: Premium promotion hides price and commitment before the CTA
findings.evidence: The mobile first viewport repeatedly promotes Unlock premium benefits / Unlock but shows no price, billing period, renewal, or cancellation terms before entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Put price, billing cadence, renewal, cancellation, and consent terms beside the premium CTA before commitment.

findings.summary: Carousel interaction uses tiny custom controls without platform snapping
findings.evidence: The UI probe found zero scroll-snap containers while the hero uses custom previous/next buttons and 8x8 indicator buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-snap for swipeable carousels and keep large, named previous/next controls as a keyboard fallback.

taskList.title: Fix accessible names, landmarks, focus, targets, contrast, and zoom
Cut first-load media, CSS, scripts, and third-party requests
Deploy security headers and secure authentication cookies
Use semantic platform controls and recovery links
Fix runtime errors and intrinsic image sizing
Complete locale coverage and indexing signals
Clarify premium pricing and commitment terms
Modernise responsive navigation and carousel motion
